promptLatex: In a survey of 80 people, 45 liked math, 35 liked physics, and 25 liked chemistry. 15 liked both math and physics, 10 liked both math and chemistry, and 8 liked both physics and chemistry. 5 liked all three subjects. How many people liked none of the three subjects?
hintLatex:
Use inclusion-exclusion for three sets.
|M ∪ P ∪ C| = |M| + |P| + |C| - |M ∩ P| - |M ∩ C| - |P ∩ C| + |M ∩ P ∩ C|.
Compute the union, then subtract from 80 to find those who liked none.
solutionLatex:
Use inclusion-exclusion for three sets M (math), P (physics), C (chemistry).

|M ∪ P ∪ C| = |M| + |P| + |C| - |M ∩ P| - |M ∩ C| - |P ∩ C| + |M ∩ P ∩ C|.

= 45 + 35 + 25 - 15 - 10 - 8 + 5 = 77.

People who liked at least one subject: 77.
People who liked none: 80 - 77 = 17.
